- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in next period; reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If true price deviates from recent 7-day average by >2%, model often fails to mean-revert; adjust forecast toward 7-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag true price by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is bullish, or delay if bearish.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.0 or vice versa), model misreads momentum; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.
